title: The Easter Vigil
hookLine: a fire in the dark, one candle, then the whole church lit, and the ancient Easter song
last: THE ONE DAY WITH NO MASS.

cards: Saturday night, after dark. The church is completely unlit. Everyone stands outside, or crowded at the back, around a fire burning in a brazier.
The priest blesses the fire and lights one tall candle from it, the Easter candle, marked with a cross, the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, and this year's numbers.
A deacon lifts it high and sings, light of Christ. Everyone answers, thanks be to God.

The flame passes from that one candle to the next person's small candle, then the next, then hundreds, until the whole dark church is glowing. Then someone steps up beside the big candle and starts to sing.

teach.b: That song is the Exsultet, the Easter Proclamation, named for its first Latin word: exsultet, let it rejoice. Let the angels of heaven rejoice, let the earth be glad, let the Church sing.
Nobody knows for sure who wrote it. It's very old, and it's sung alone, usually by a deacon, in candlelight.
It's long, with a refrain that keeps coming back like a drumbeat: this is the night. The night God led Israel out of Egypt through the sea. The night the pillar of fire drove out the darkness.
The night Christ broke the chains of death and rose from the grave. The sea, the fire and the tomb, gathered into one night. Then a startling line.
Speaking of Adam's sin, it sings, in Latin, O felix culpa: O happy fault, that earned for us so great a Redeemer. It dares to call the first sin happy, because of where the story went.
And, lovely detail, it thanks the bees: the candle is beeswax, and the song praises the work of the mother bee who made it.
After the Exsultet come the readings, up to seven from the Old Testament, walking through the whole story from creation. Then the Gloria, every bell ringing again after two days of silence.
The alleluia returns. And adults who have been preparing are baptized and confirmed that night. Augustine called this vigil the mother of all vigils.

how: Catholics keep the Easter Vigil after nightfall on Holy Saturday: the new fire and the Easter candle, the Exsultet sung in candlelight, a series of readings, the Gloria and the alleluia returning, and the baptism and confirmation of adults entering the Church.

games.q: you're holding an unlit candle in a dark church. the deacon has just sung light of Christ. what happens next?

games.why: every candle is lit from the one Easter candle, passed from neighbor to neighbor, until the whole church glows.

practice: Turn off the lights in your room, now or tonight, and light one candle, or a phone screen turned low if a candle isn't safe. Watch how far one small flame reaches, what it lights and what it doesn't.
If you pray, answer as the church does at the vigil, thanks be to God; if you don't, simply watch the light and let the dark around it be quiet.

wordCard.voice: Exsultet. Let it rejoice. The ancient Easter song, sung beside one candle in a dark church. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: let it rejoice, the first word of the Easter Proclamation.
